questions.question: What is the auxiliary space complexity of a tail-recursive function optimized by a compiler using Tail Call Optimization (TCO)?

questions.question: Which of the following functions is TAIL recursive?
options: A) int f(n) { if(n==0) return 1; return n*f(n-1); }
B) int f(n, acc) { if(n==0) return acc; return f(n-1, n*acc); }
C) int f(n) { if(n==0) return 0; return f(n-1) + f(n-2); }
D) int f(n) { if(n==0) return 1; return 1 + f(n-1); }
questions.explanation: Option B is tail recursive because the final statement is purely a recursive call with no pending arithmetic operation.

questions.question: In recursive binary search, what is the space complexity due to function call stack for array of size N?
questions.explanation: Recursive depth of binary search is bounded by the height of decision tree, which is log2(N).

questions.question: How many total moves are required to solve Tower of Hanoi problem for 6 disks recursively?
questions.explanation: Tower of Hanoi requires T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1 moves, resulting in total (2^n - 1) moves. For n=6, moves = 63.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort recursive partition when pivot is always smallest element?
questions.explanation: When pivot is worst, recurrence becomes T(n) = T(n-1) + O(n), solving to O(n^2).

questions.question: What is indirect recursion?

questions.explanation: Indirect recursion occurs when two or more functions invoke each other in a cyclic structure.

questions.question: Which traversal of a binary search tree (BST) uses recursion to produce elements in sorted ascending order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal (Left, Root, Right) on BST prints nodes in ascending sorted order.

questions.question: What is overlapping subproblems property in recursion?

questions.explanation: Overlapping subproblems mean recursive tree computes same values repeatedly, making it ideal for memoization/DP.
